what: What each of the far-court pilot's 36 human clicks actually landed on, classified BY EYE at 5x zoom against the frame the labeller saw. Same role as data/gold/false_lock_classes.json: the classification is the evidence, the contact sheet is regenerable.
method: py tools/farcourt_labels_to_dataset.py --clip farcourt_pilot --contact-sheet data/output/farcourt_pilot_clicks.jpg, then one verdict per tile.
caveat: One observer, one pass, n=36. The split it supports (a click is on a ball, or on background) is coarse and was obvious at this zoom; the finer class names are descriptive, not load-bearing.
notes: Frame 30/31 (yt_rz4T0-VALNw) are counted as real_ball although the click is 39-47 px from the tracker's prior: the human found the ball and the TRACKER was wrong. Any metric scored as 'agreement with the tracker' counts these as failures, which is why the classification is by eye.
Frames 0/1/2 landed on the score digits and panel body of yt_6jp23ghDY9Q, and 7/8 on the panel of yt_RZ_wyJ9rI3Q. Neither is the 'tennis-ball icon' that data/output/farcourt_label_yield.md describes.
yt_8-BkpjFFIhQ (frames 3/4/5) and yt_WjHZrIYteDA (15/16/17) carry NO burned-in graphic. farcourt_label_yield.md lists both as HUD clips.
